references.text: Psalm 23 describes the Lord as a shepherd who leads and provides for his sheep, an image that Jesus clarifies and fulfills when he identifies himself as the good shepherd.
Ezekiel 34:11-16 contains God's promise to seek out and save his scattered sheep himself, a prophecy that Jesus confirms by laying down his life for them.
Isaiah 53:7 describes the Messiah as a lamb led to slaughter who does not open his mouth, a direct image of the good shepherd who voluntarily gives his life for the sheep.
Ezekiel 34:23-24 predicts that God will raise up one shepherd, David, to tend the people, a prophecy that Jesus fulfills when he says, 'I am the good shepherd.'
1 Peter 5:4 refers to the 'chief Shepherd' who will come and give an eternal reward, a direct link to Jesus as the good shepherd who gives his life for the sheep.
Revelation 7:17 describes the Lamb in the midst of the throne who will shepherd them, an eschatological fulfillment of Jesus as the good shepherd who cares for his own.
